top_stories.title: Building self-improving tax agents with Codex
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has published a case study on building self-improving tax agents using Codex, its AI coding tool. The post details how the system iterates and improves its own performance over time, representing a practical application of agentic AI in a professional domain. This is a primary-source update from OpenAI on a concrete generative AI deployment.

top_stories.title: Millions of AI agents imperiled by critical vulnerability in open source package
top_stories.summary: A critical security vulnerability in a widely used open source package is putting millions of AI agents at risk, according to Ars Technica. The flaw could be exploited to compromise AI agent pipelines built on the affected software. The discovery highlights growing security concerns as agentic AI deployments scale rapidly.

top_stories.title: Robinhood will let your AI agent trade stocks and make (or lose) lots of money
top_stories.summary: Robinhood is introducing AI agent-powered stock trading, allowing automated systems to execute trades on behalf of users. The move marks a significant step toward autonomous financial decision-making for retail investors. The feature raises questions about risk, oversight, and accountability in AI-driven investing.

top_stories.title: Fake academic journals are publishing AI-generated papers under real professors' names
top_stories.summary: Fraudulent academic journals are using AI to generate fake research papers attributed to real professors without their knowledge, according to a newly surfaced report. The practice poses serious risks to research integrity and academic publishing. The trend underscores the growing misuse of generative AI in scholarly contexts.

top_stories.title: Rethinking organizational design in the age of agentic AI
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review examines how businesses are restructuring their organisations in response to the rise of agentic AI systems. The piece explores how AI agents are changing workflows, team structures, and decision-making hierarchies within enterprises. It draws on emerging research and practitioner experience to outline practical implications for business leaders.

further_links.title: Former Google and Apple Researchers Launch a Startup to Build AI's Missing Feedback Loop [Metered]
further_links.summary: Ex-researchers from Google and Apple have founded a startup aiming to build AI systems that improve through ongoing user interaction, addressing a key limitation of current models.

further_links.title: YouTube is putting AI labels where you'll actually see them
further_links.summary: YouTube is updating its AI content labelling system so that disclosures about AI-generated or AI-altered content appear more prominently, including on Shorts.

further_links.title: Why the Vatican Invited Anthropic to the Pope's AI Encyclical Presentation [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired reports on how Anthropic came to be present at the Vatican's presentation of Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical addressing AI, offering insight into the Church's engagement with AI companies.

further_links.title: What Pope Leo XIV's First Encyclical Says About the Power of AI [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired analyses the key arguments in Pope Leo XIV's encyclical on AI, which calls for human dignity to be protected as artificial intelligence reshapes society and labour.

further_links.title: The AI fight brewing inside The New York Times
further_links.summary: The New York Times Tech Guild is pushing back against management proposals to use AI tools to monitor employee performance, marking an emerging labour flashpoint over AI in the newsroom.

further_links.title: The AI bubble isn't like the internet bubble
further_links.summary: Cory Doctorow argues on Pluralistic that the current AI investment bubble differs structurally from the dot-com bubble in ways that could make its eventual correction more damaging.

further_links.title: Mid-Market Companies Lose an Average of 25% of Their AI Budget Before Seeing a Single Return, New Freshworks Research Finds
further_links.summary: New research from Freshworks finds that mid-market firms are wasting a quarter of their AI budgets before achieving any measurable return, pointing to implementation and strategy failures.

further_links.title: The Download: puncturing the AI jobs panic [Metered]
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review looks at new data that complicates the narrative of widespread AI-driven job displacement, suggesting the reality is more nuanced than headlines suggest.

further_links.title: AI tried to bury this politician — now people have actually heard of him
further_links.summary: A New York politician whose campaign was targeted by AI-generated negative content found that the AI-fuelled controversy ultimately raised his public profile rather than diminishing it.

further_links.title: CIOs are enlisting business users to vibe code their own apps
further_links.summary: Enterprise CIOs are increasingly encouraging non-technical business users to build their own internal applications using AI coding tools, a trend sometimes called 'vibe coding'.

ethan_mollick.title: Choosing to Stay Human
ethan_mollick.summary: Ethan Mollick explores the question of when and why people might choose to retain human involvement in tasks that AI could perform, arguing that this is increasingly a deliberate and meaningful choice rather than a default. He examines the personal, social, and ethical dimensions of deciding which activities should remain human-led. The post encourages readers to think carefully about where human effort and presence still matters.
